Notation\\n\\n- `\u03a3` \u2014 the set of Unicode code points (Python `str` characters); `String = \u03a3*`.\\n- `\u2124` \u2014 the mathematical integers, with the standard operations `+`, `\u2212`, `\u00d7`.\\n- Token lists are finite sequences; `\u03b5` is the empty list, `\u00b7` is list\\n  concatenation, `head(t)` the first element.\\n- `{ x }` in EBNF means zero or more repetitions of `x`.\\n- `\u21d3` is the token-coverage relation defined in \u00a77.\\n- All defining equations below are definitional axioms of the semantics.\\n\\n## 3. No other exception may escape for `str` inputs\\n  within the resource envelope of \u00a712.\\n- **C4 (Messages).** Exception *messages* are not contractual. Indicative\\n  strings of the reference implementation:\\n\\n  | Condition                                   | Indicative message                     |\\n  |---------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|\\n  | invalid character `c` at 0-based index `i`  | `Invalid character {c!r} at position {i}` |\\n  | operand expected at end of input            | `Unexpected end of expression`         |\\n  | token where an operand was expected         | `Unexpected token {tok!r}`             |\\n  | group not closed                            | `Missing closing parenthesis`          |\\n  | leftover tokens after the top-level `expr`  | `Unexpected token {tok!r}`             |\\n\\n  **[N]** The reference implementation lexes the whole string before parsing,\\n  so a lex error anywhere in `s` is reported even where a parse error would\\n  occur earlier positionally. Verification obligations\\n\\nAn implementation conforms to this specification iff it satisfies C1\u2013C4 and\\nproperties P1\u2013P9 below.
